crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Prior Art and Clearance Searching
children.blurb: Prior art and clearance searching covers patentability, validity, freedom to operate, and trademark availability checks before filing or launch.

children.name: Trademark Filing and Specimens
children.blurb: Trademark filing and specimens covers the preparation, submission, and evidentiary support of trademark applications, including identification of goods and services, classification, and proof of use in commerce.

children.name: Licensing Synthetic Assets and Likeness
children.blurb: This page covers how organizations license rights in AI-generated or AI-modified assets and in synthetic representations of a person's voice, face, or persona.

children.name: Patent Claim Drafting
children.blurb: Patent claim drafting is the process of writing the numbered claims that define the legal scope of protection in a patent application.

children.name: Infringement Detection and Enforcement
children.blurb: Infringement detection and enforcement covers identifying unauthorized use of protected marks, copyrighted works, patents, trade dress, and other intellectual property across digital and physical channels.

sections.body: This field covers how artificial intelligence is used in intellectual property work and how IP law applies to AI outputs. Clearance searching uses machine learning to compare a proposed mark or invention against large databases of existing trademarks and patents. Trademark filing tools generate specimen images and classify goods and services. Licensing work addresses synthetic assets and likeness rights, including AI-generated voices and images. Patent claim drafting uses language models to propose claim language, and infringement detection scans products, code, or media for matches to protected works.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Clearance searching is fairly mature for text and logo similarity, but it still misses conceptual similarity and foreign language nuance. Trademark filing tools can draft descriptions and generate specimens, yet examiners still reject many AI-prepared filings over issues like specimen authenticity. Licensing synthetic assets is unsettled because courts have not fully resolved who owns an AI-generated voice or image, and likeness rights vary by state. Patent claim drafting can produce plausible text but often fails on enablement and definiteness, so human review remains necessary. Infringement detection works well for exact copies and near matches, but it is weaker for paraphrased code, style imitation, and fair use judgments. Of the 142 active AI lawsuits this site tracks, 92 are intellectual property disputes, which shows how much is still being litigated rather than settled.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from early-stage searching to enforcement. Prior Art and Clearance Searching is where a reader starts to see how AI finds existing patents and trademarks before filing. Trademark Filing and Specimens covers the actual application work, including AI-generated specimens and class choices. Licensing Synthetic Assets and Likeness sits in the middle because it deals with rights that are not yet fully defined, such as AI voices and digital personas. Patent Claim Drafting is the page for how language models propose claim language and where those drafts fail. Infringement Detection and Enforcement closes the loop by showing how AI monitors for unauthorized use and what happens after a match is found.
